name: PreOperativeAssessment
title: Pre-operative Assessment
description: Completed by patients before a planned surgery or procedure, for the pre-admission and anesthesia team.

extension.valueMarkdown: Reviewed by the pre-admission nurse and the anesthesiologist before the day of surgery.

item.text: This form helps your anesthesia and surgical team plan a safe procedure. Please answer every question as accurately as you can.
What type of anesthesia were you told to expect?
It's fine if you don't know. Your anesthesiologist will discuss it with you.
Are you expected to stay overnight?
Is there any chance you could be pregnant?
Have you had general anesthesia or sedation before?
Did you have any of these afterwards?

valueCoding.display: Confusion lasting more than a day

item.text: Has a blood relative had a serious reaction to anesthesia, such as a very high fever?
Some reactions to anesthesia run in families, for example malignant hyperthermia.
Please make sure you tell your anesthesiologist about this before your surgery.
Do you have any of these?

valueCoding.display: Stiff neck or limited neck movement

item.text: Have you been diagnosed with sleep apnea?
Do you use a CPAP or BiPAP machine?
If yes, please bring your machine on the day of surgery.
How often do you feel tired or sleepy during the day?
Do you have, or have you ever had, any of these?
Blood clots in the legs or lungs
Can you climb two flights of stairs without stopping?

valueCoding.display: No, because of chest pain or shortness of breath

item.text: This tells us how well your heart and lungs cope with exertion.
About how many blocks can you walk before you need to rest?
Do you have a pacemaker, defibrillator or other implanted device?

valueCoding.display: I quit in the last 8 weeks

item.text: Stopping smoking even a few days before surgery lowers the risk of breathing problems.
Do you take any of these blood thinners?
When did you last take it?
Do not stop a blood thinner on your own. Your surgeon or doctor will tell you if and when to stop it.
Do you take any herbal medicines or supplements?
Some supplements affect bleeding or anesthesia, so we need to know about them too.
Are you allergic to any of these?
Latex allergy: your operating room will be prepared latex-free.
With a BMI of 40 or more, your anesthesiologist may want to see you before the day of surgery.
Follow the eating and drinking instructions your care team gives you exactly. If you eat or drink when you should not, your surgery may be postponed for your safety.
Will someone stay with you for the first 24 hours?
What time were you asked to arrive?
How should we update your family on the day?

valueCoding.display: In person in the waiting room

item.text: I will follow the eating and drinking instructions I am given
I will take only the medications I am told to take on the morning of surgery
I will remove jewelry, piercings and nail polish
